title: Reviewer scope
description: What one architecture reviewer is handed as its `review scope`: the Epic's review scope (what `atw-matrix review-scope` prints) narrowed to the criteria the reviewer's groups cover. The check step (orchestrator/flows/architecture_check.py) writes it, one file per reviewer, and validates it against this file. Nothing outside it is the reviewer's to review.

epic.description: The id of the Epic's entry in the matrix.

groups.description: The reviewer groups of effective-architecture/review-criteria.json that selected the reviewer.

criteria.description: The ids of the criteria the reviewer reviews against; their text and level are in effective-architecture/review-standard.md.

requirements.description: The Epic's requirements: each requirement entry's id and its name, which is the PRD heading that states it. When `prd` is set, read only these headings of the PRD, and only those a check needs.

documents.description: The arc42 documents the Epic reaches that are not effective, each with the headings reached; for a `no-change-needed` conclusion also the effective documents and headings the architect cites as meeting the Epic (lifecycle `effective`). Empty when no group of the reviewer covers documents.

trd.description: The TRD's path when a group of the reviewer covers its requirements; null otherwise.

prd.description: The PRD's path when the review checks content against the Epic's requirements: the TRD's coverage, or a `no-change-needed` conclusion. Null otherwise; the brief then hands no PRD.

signals.description: The lists of the architect's result (architecture-result.schema.json, reviewSignals) that selected the reviewer, by name.

id.description: The document's matrix id, `document:<path under the architecture root>`.

lifecycle.description: The document's lifecycle state from its front matter.

headings.description: The headings reached, sorted and without repeats; review these.

reachedBy.description: The relationships through which the Epic reaches the document.

entry.description: The requirement the document covers, or the feature or added or changed element it describes.

heading.description: The heading the relationship names; empty when it names none.
